decisions.reason: The existing message-118 MODIFY already captures the stronger accent-specific effect: the É accent is the Hero V's literal terminal section, with the obsolete accent form removed.
The unified terminal gesture changes letter geometry, not the deferred champagne-metal material treatment or its role.
The existing message-118 MODIFY already preserves the earlier Option 2 Hero V as the geometry foundation; the shared terminal rule is separately owned by the source Requirement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

Please continue refining the system from the hero V in Option 2 from the preceding round, which I have attached again for reference, rather than from the updated hero V included in this presentation. That earlier silhouette remains the strongest foundation. As you develop it, apply one governing rule across the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent: each must carry a completely unified terminal gesture.

Bringing all three forms into one view was exactly the right next step because it confirmed that we are now refining a shared architectural language, not a single isolated letter. It also revealed that the É accent should not merely take inspiration from the hero V; it needs to be the hero V’s literal termination.

More specifically, imagine removing the last part of the hero V’s right arm, lifting it intact, and positioning that exact gesture above the É. That is the relationship I want. I believe such consistency will make the Veillvé identity genuinely proprietary, and once the gesture is fully unified across the three forms, I think we will have created something truly special.

value_updates.relationship_to_hero_v: grows from the Hero V geometry and shares its angles, proportions, material language, and completely unified terminal gesture

decisions.reason: The source refines the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent system but does not change or resume the deferred internal wordmark letterforms.
The terminal unification rule does not alter the deferred complete-wordmark kerning, rhythm, or visual hierarchy requirements.
The statement that terminal consistency will support a proprietary identity is rationale for the geometric rule and does not change the existing brand-expression state.
The source does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
